title: Note Rate Record Error: Larkspur's Share of a Closing and Funding Per Diem Shortfall
content:
Under the Closing and Funding product, Larkspur absorbs part of a per diem shortfall that its closing record's note rate created. The allowance compares the closing record with the borrower's Rate Lock Commitment: the rate the lock holds, and the lock's relock entries (relock fee bookings among the lock's pricing entries) with their dates.

**Rule.** Where the closing record's note rate differs from the rate the lock holds and the lock carries a relock entry dated after the closing record was opened, Larkspur absorbs 7.50; where the closing record's note rate differs from the rate the lock holds and no such relock entry exists, it absorbs 5.00; otherwise it absorbs nothing for the rate. Amounts are in US dollars. Any record-error allowance comes off the per diem shortfall first, the remainder rounded half up to the cent and never below zero.

| Note rate on the closing record vs. rate the lock holds | Relock entry dated after the closing record was opened? | Larkspur absorbs |
|---|---|---|
| differs | Yes | 7.50 |
| differs | No (no relock entry, or only relock entries dated on or before the opening date) | 5.00 |
| same | either | nothing |

## Example (hypothetical)

A closing record opened on 4 March shows a note rate of 6.25 percent while the lock holds 6.5 percent. A relock entry dated 11 March gives 7.50; with the only relock entry dated 1 March, it is 5.00; with the closing record showing 6.5 percent, nothing is absorbed for the rate.
